put.summary: Set / reset the admin-user password for an Xcloud instance
put.description: Encrypts the password at rest (AES-256-GCM) and resets `password_provisioned_at` so the worker re-applies it inside the guest on the next password-inject tick. The password is never returned — the DTO exposes only `adminPasswordSet` and the provisioning timestamps.

put.summary: Replace the security-group set for an Xcloud instance
put.description: Replaces the VM's assigned security groups (a list of SG names in the tenant namespace). Patches the live VM spec (`VirtualMachineSpec.security_groups`) — applied without a stopped-state precondition; upstream reconciles the NIC firewall for running and stopped VMs alike — then mirrors the value onto the instance row. When the VM has not been created upstream yet (status `pending`), only the row is updated and the worker applies the set at create time.

post.summary: Queue a suspend-to-disk action
post.description: Saves the guest's memory to disk and stops the VM (upstream desired state `SUSPEND`), so it frees CPU/RAM while keeping its running state. Resume with the normal start endpoint — upstream restores the guest from disk instead of cold-booting it.

post.summary: Queue a boot-mode change (recovery / normal)
post.description: Sets the upstream `spec.boot_into_recovery` flag. macOS guests come up in recoveryOS while it is set; upstream ignores it for Linux guests. **Applying it restarts the VM** — a boot-mode change is a config change upstream, so the node recreates the VM.

recovery.description: true → the guest boots into recoveryOS; false → normal boot. Applying the change restarts the VM.

patch.summary: Update a tenant Xcloud image's labels
patch.description: Full-replace of the customer-controlled label slots on a tenant-namespace image. Worker-internal labels (`source`/`digest`/`precache`) are preserved verbatim from the upstream read. Platform catalog images (`source: default`) are read-only — attempts to patch them return 403.

delete.description: Removes a tenant-namespace image record (idempotent — already-gone collapses to 204). Platform catalog images (`source: default`) remain read-only. By default the OCI manifest is also deleted from the registry for tenant-only images. Managed registry images use tenant-scoped repository deletion without customer-supplied registry credentials. Deletion is refused if the tag has moved to a different digest or the manifest is shared. An external public registry (ghcr.io, Docker Hub, …) is deleted directly; an internal registry (private VPC address, *.internal) is reached through the regional cloud agent (the `registry` gateway service), so such a region must have a `registry` service configured — otherwise the delete fails with 412. Deletion is rejected when another image in the same tenant namespace is known to reference the same manifest digest.

schema.description: When `false`, remove only the tenant catalog entry and leave registry bytes untouched. Defaults to `true` (delete manifest).

get.description: Union of the tenant namespace catalog and the cluster-wide `default` namespace. `source: tenant` networks are already seeded and can be used immediately; `source: default` networks are lazily seeded on the next VM-create.

post.summary: Create a network in the tenant Xcloud namespace
post.description: Customer self-service: provisions a network in the tenant namespace of the target region. Names already present in the cluster-wide `default` catalog are reserved (the seeder would otherwise re-create them on the next VM-create, masking the custom spec). Admin-managed `default` entries appear as `source: 'default'` in the list endpoint and stay editable only through the admin region surface.

delete.description: Refuses the delete when the same name exists in the cluster `default` catalog (it would just be re-seeded on the next VM-create — operator must remove the default first), or when any non-terminal VM in the region still references the network.

post.summary: Run a command inside the VM via the in-guest xcloud-agent
post.description: Executes `argv` inside the instance and streams the result as `application/x-ndjson`: one JSON object per line — `{"stream":"stdout"|"stderr","data":"<base64>"}` frames terminated by exactly one `{"exit":{"code":<int>,"timedOut":<bool>,"error":"<str>"}}` line. Pre-stream failures are ordinary ProblemDetails JSON bodies; once the first NDJSON byte is written the status line is already 200.

home.description: Absolute directory that `cwd` must stay below. When set, a `cwd` outside it fails the command with exit 1 instead of running it elsewhere. Confinement is lexical: a symlink inside the guest pointing outward is not caught here.

pty.description: Not supported. `true` is rejected with 422 rather than ignored.

200.description: NDJSON stream of stdout/stderr frames terminated by a single exit frame.
